issues.legal_issue: A subsequent proceeding seeking to set aside a court sale is not barred by res judicata when it rests on a new statutory right that could not have been invoked in the earlier proceeding.
material_facts: An earlier application to set aside the sale was dismissed finally under a law whose relevant restriction did not apply because the property had been attached before the date specified by that law.
A later enactment provided a broader basis for setting aside transfers of evacuee property made under court orders, and the sale fell within its scope.
The later proceeding concerned the same parties and property and sought the same relief, but relied on the new statutory basis, which had not been available when the earlier application was decided.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent proceeding was not barred by res judicata, and the ruling setting aside the court sale was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including Explanation IV, res judicata requires consideration of the court's competence, the parties, the matters in issue, matters that ought to have been raised, and the final decision. The subsequent claim must rest on the same cause of action as the former proceeding, and the applicant must have had an opportunity to obtain the relief earlier. Section 8(2) of the East Punjab Evacuees’ (Administration of Property) Act, 1947, had a narrower scope than section 17(2) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1949; the latter created a new right to challenge a wider class of court-ordered transfers. Section 17(2) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, as substituted retrospectively by the 1951 Amendment Act, was materially similar for this issue. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: evacuee_property_sale_challenge and prior_final_decision and same_parties_and_property and transfer_within_new_law_scope and relief_unavailable_under_old_law

predicates.evacuee_property_sale_challenge: The proceeding seeks to set aside a court sale of property treated as evacuee property.
predicates.prior_final_decision: An earlier proceeding concerning the sale ended in a final decision.
predicates.same_parties_and_property: The earlier and later proceedings involve the same parties and property.
predicates.transfer_within_new_law_scope: The court-ordered transfer falls within the broader class of transfers that a later law permits the applicant to challenge.
predicates.relief_unavailable_under_old_law: The applicant could not have obtained the relief sought in the later proceeding under the law applicable when the earlier proceeding was decided.

issues.definition: When a final decision has already been made between the same parties concerning the same property, a later challenge to the sale is not barred if it falls within a new legal basis and that relief was unavailable under the earlier law.

issues.legal_issue: A later application expressly invoking a new statutory ground may be considered even when it is consolidated with an earlier application seeking the same relief.
material_facts: The Custodian filed an application after the new ordinance had come into force that expressly referred to its provision authorizing a challenge to the sale.
The court restored an earlier application that had been dismissed for default, consolidated the applications, and disposed of them together.
issues.conclusion: A fresh application invoking the new statutory ground had been made, and the contention that no such application existed was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The court examined the later application and the order disposing of the consolidated applications and found an express reference to section 17(2) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1949. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.evacuee_property_sale_challenge: The proceeding seeks to set aside a court sale of property treated as evacuee property.
predicates.later_application_invokes_new_ground: The applicant filed a later application that expressly invoked a newly available legal ground for challenging the sale.
predicates.applications_considered_together: The court restored or considered the earlier application together with the later application and disposed of them together.

issues.definition: When a later application expressly invokes a new ground and is considered together with an earlier application, the new-ground application was before the court.
